title: Signal-led experiment convergence and contamination budget
creator: Rohit Singh
description:
Goal: Define a repeatable rubric for determining when an experiment has 'converged' (sufficient evidence to promote or rollback) and establish a contamination budget that limits cross-experiment signal bleed for top-line and safety metrics.

Context: As Redwood scales experiments across Dedicated, Hosted, and Private customers we see more parallel canaries and A/B forks. Existing gates focus on single-metric thresholds and percentage traffic rules, but we lack a concise convergence definition and a contamination accounting approach. This makes rollouts brittle (false positives/negatives) and increases the chance of noisy upstream regressions.

Scope: This ticket is a PM-led deliverable to define the convergence rubric, contamination budget model, and operational checklist for staging and promoting experiment waves. Deliverables will include: a short PRD, evaluation milestone definitions, monitoring templates, and a lightweight escalation ladder for edge cases. Engineering will implement metric hooks and tagging; Design will validate rollout UX for canary controls in Console.

Non-goals: Building automatic rollback automation (out of scope) and re-architecting the entire metrics stack. Those can be follow-ups.

M4: Cross-functional review and sign-off (Eng, Design, SRE, Legal) - due 2025-12-09
M5: Playbook & rollout checklist published in Confluence - due 2025-12-15
acceptance_criteria: A1: Convergence rubric document describing primary vs guardrail signals, minimum sample sizes, and minimum observation windows
A2: Contamination budget model that quantifies acceptable signal bleed across concurrent experiments and enforces per-customer experiment caps
A3: Instrumentation checklist with required tags (experiment_id, cohort, upstream_changes) and a Console widget prototype for contamination heatmap
A4: Runbook with explicit roll/hold/rollback decision rules and escalation contacts
A5: Sign-off from SRE on sample size/latency impact and from Legal if the model affects customer traffic assignments
metrics_and_signals: Primary metric: top-level quality score (redwood_quality.v1) with delta and CI
Trust signals: sample size, funnel completion rates, synthetic-check pass rate
plan: Week 1: Collate historic experiment outcomes and identify common failure modes (bias from cold-starts, traffic shifts, metric suppression)
Week 2: Draft convergence thresholds — combine frequentist p-value gate with minimum practical effect size and holdout stability window
Week 3: Define contamination budget mechanics (per-org budget, lifetime credit, decay model) and simple accounting rules
Week 4: Prototype Console contamination heatmap and review instrumentation gaps with Eng
Week 5: Publish playbook and run tabletop exercises with SRE/SEs
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly strict convergence rules block beneficial rollouts — Mitigation: include a pragmatic fast-track clause for P0 customer fixes
Risk: Contamination model complexity causes low adoption — Mitigation: default to conservative presets and enable advanced knobs for power users
Risk: Instrumentation gaps lead to blind spots — Mitigation: include a mandatory QA checklist before any experiment wave
Risk: Conflicting metrics across teams — Mitigation: require a single canonical primary metric per experiment and a documented rationale
